import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_2.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']

# Step 1: Join source1 and source2 on 'movie_id' to get ratings with movie titles
ratings_with_titles = pd.merge(source1, source2[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join the above result with source0 on 'user_id' to get gender info for each rating
ratings_full = pd.merge(ratings_with_titles, source0[['user_id', 'gender']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 3: We want to produce the target table with schema ['title', 'F', 'M']
# 'F' and 'M' are average ratings by female and male users respectively for each title

# Filter ratings by gender and compute average rating per title
avg_ratings = ratings_full.groupby(['title', 'gender'])['rating'].mean().reset_index()

# Pivot the table to have columns 'F' and 'M' with average ratings
pivot_table = avg_ratings.pivot(index='title', columns='gender', values='rating').reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema
pivot_table = pivot_table.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Some titles might have ratings from only one gender, fill missing values with NaN
pivot_table['F'] = pivot_table['F'].astype(float)
pivot_table['M'] = pivot_table['M'].astype(float)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_df = pivot_table[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Save the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on movie_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 and the above join on user_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Compute mean rating by gender per title
# Pivot table approach: group by title and gender, aggregate mean rating
pivot = joined_all.groupby(['title', 'gender'])['rating'].mean().unstack()

# Rename columns to match target schema: 'F' and 'M'
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Reset index to have 'title' as a column
result = pivot.reset_index()

# Write to target CSV with exact column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_16/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
